cars.variant: Adventurer S-26 345 dual-carb hardtop — 1957 USA revised AMA, TorqueFlite
cars.specification_market: 1957 USA S-26 Adventurer two-door hardtop, nominal 345 Hemi with dual carburettors and standard TorqueFlite, using revised December 1956 factory AMA sheets. Count the original 1956–1960 Adventurer performance-road programme once across years, engines and bodies, with associated Fireflite identities reviewed together. Not a 1954 Ghia concept or a later wedge/fuel-injected engine. Preserve native advertised bhp and factory test convention; do not claim an unqualified world-first, modern net conversion, measured acceleration, racing camshaft, curb mass or hardtop dimensions from default sedan tables.
cars.summary: The Adventurer is a significant early American performance programme: its 1957 factory-standard dual-carb Hemi advertised 345 brake horsepower from a nominal 345 cubic inches. This engineering benchmark and the programme’s continuing recognition in specialist museum collections justify its place beyond rarity, luxury trim or price.

sources.publisher: DeSoto Division, Chrysler Corporation / Over-Drive facsimile
sources.title: 1957 DeSoto AMA Consolidated Specification Questionnaire — revised 15 December 1956
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer AMA specification sheets, hosted scan
sources.notes: 25-page scanned file, 5,224,404 bytes despite filename 1-24. Full indexes 0, 1, 5, 12, 14 and 18 visually read; S-26 Adventurer column and footnotes distinguished from ordinary S-26 Fireflite and S-27 Firesweep. Sheets 1–2 establish standard engine and ratings under their stated SAE Engine Test Code accessories convention. Sheet 6 identifies two Carter four-barrels, 13 TorqueFlite, 15 wheels and brakes. Sheet 19 states Adventurer body data refer to a special club coupe, two-door hardtop. No measured displacement or unqualified priority claim inferred.
